title: Whose Agent Are You? Multi-Layer Fingerprinting and Attribution of Autonomous Web Agents
abstract: arXiv:2606.20910v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As AI web agents proliferate, combining large language models with autonomous, browser-level control, indiscriminate content scraping by web agents has emerged as a privacy and security challenge. Existing defenses, such as robots.txt and active bot-blocking, are insufficient, as they are widely violated and easily circumvented. In this work, we demonstrate that AI web agents can be effectively distinguished from humans and traditional crawlers using a multi-layer fingerprint based on both network layer characteristics (e.g., TLS, HTTP) and browser interaction behavior. We implement this mechanism as a programmatic logging framework that can be deployed on a live, instrumented domain. translated_title: 你是谁的智能体？自主网页智能体的多层指纹识别与归因
translated_abstract: 随着结合大语言模型与自主浏览器级控制能力的AI网页智能体不断增多，智能体不加区分地抓取内容已成为一个隐私与安全挑战。现有的防御手段，例如robots.txt和主动的机器人拦截，并不足够，因为它们被广泛违反且容易被绕过。在这项工作中，我们证明了基于网络层特征（如TLS、HTTP）和浏览器交互行为的多层指纹，可以有效地将AI网页智能体与人类用户及传统爬虫区分开来。我们将这一机制实现为一个可编程的日志框架，能够部署在实际运行的、经过监测的域名上。通过分析六个主流的智能体框架（AutoGen、Browser Use、Claude、Gemini、ChatGPT和Skyvern），我们揭示了这些系统在组装HTTP请求、建立TLS/HTTP连接以及执行自主浏览操作方面的潜在结构性差异……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一种结合网络层特征（TLS/HTTP）与浏览器交互行为的多层指纹方法，能够有效区分AI网页智能体与人类用户及传统爬虫，并可对AutoGen、Browser Use、Claude、Gemini、ChatGPT和Skyvern等六大主流智能体框架进行归因识别。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a multi-layer fingerprinting approach that combines network-layer characteristics (TLS/HTTP) with browser interaction behavior to effectively distinguish AI web agents from humans and traditional crawlers, enabling attribution of six major agent frameworks including AutoGen, Browser Use, Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Skyvern.
